title: III–V: necessity of end, of agent, and of idea
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): therefore it is not intrinsic necessity as formal — whence other nations have other letters plus other vocabularies — but because it can hold itself otherwise toward ye artisan's pleasure — plus this necessity concurs somehow with formal. V. Necessity from idea is that by which according toward God's or humankind's idea things so hold themselves that they cannot hold otherwise. IV. Necessity from ye agent is likewise double, violent plus natural. III. Necessity belonging toward ye end is double, either simply or toward ye better — faith is necessary simply toward salvation according toward ye Gospel's preaching.  Simply necessary toward salvation according toward the Gospel preaching is faith alone whereas knowledge of the holy languages and reading of sacred letters are toward the better because without faith nobody is saved but without those helps one may still be saved though not so well. Violent necessity appears when that rich man of the Gospel is dragged into Gehenna against his will inclination while natural necessity appears when his spirit is moved by musical sound because spirit by nature is movable and invited by sound toward its proper operation. Dry wood kindled shows necessity partly violent partly natural inasmuch as dry it is disposed by heat to receive more heat yet inasmuch as wood to be burned is against its nature. Necessity from idea explains why two and three make five and why number progresses to ten among us yet not among all nations for among some Africans it does not pass six and why letters and syllables are formed thus among this or that people and not otherwise. This necessity concurs somehow with the formal yet because it can hold otherwise at the artisan pleasure whence other nations have other letters and vocabularies it is not intrinsic necessity as the formal is.
pass_b_english: III. Necessity of the end is twofold: either simply, or unto the better. So unto salvation, according to the preaching of the Gospel, faith is necessary simply; but knowledge of the holy languages and reading of the sacred letters are unto the better — because without faith no one is saved; without these one is saved, though not so well.

IV. Necessity from the agent is likewise twofold: violent and natural. Violent, as when that rich man of the Gospel is dragged into Gehenna against the inclination of his will. Natural, when the rich man's spirit is moved by musical sound, because spirit is by nature movable and is invited by sound to its proper operation. And necessity is partly violent and partly natural when dry wood is kindled — inasmuch as dry it is disposed by heat to receive more heat, but inasmuch as wood, to be burned is against its nature.

V. Necessity from idea is that by which, according to the idea of God or of humankind, things so hold themselves that they cannot hold otherwise. Hence two and three make five, and number progresses to ten among us, yet not among all nations — for among some Africans it does not pass six. Hence also letters and syllables are so formed among this or that people and not otherwise. And this necessity concurs somehow with the formal; but because it can hold itself otherwise at the artisan's pleasure — whence other nations have other letters and other words — therefore it is not intrinsic necessity as the formal is.
source_text: III. Necessitas finis est duplex, vel simpliciter vel ad melius. Sic ad salutem, iuxta concionem Evangelii, fides necessaria est simpliciter: notitia vero linguarum sanctarum et lectio sacrarum litterarum propter melius, quia sine illa nemo servatur; sine his servatur, etsi non ita bene. IV. Necessitas ab agente itidem duplex est, violenta et naturalis. Violenta, ut cum epulo ille evangelicus rapitur in gehennam contra voluntatis suae inclinationem. Naturalis, cum spiritus epulonis a sono musico movetur, quia natura mobilis est spiritus et a sono invitatur ad propriam operationem. Ex parte vero violenta et ex parte naturalis est necessitas cum lignum aridum ignitur, quia quatenus aridum est a calore dispositum ad plus caloris recipiendum, quatenus vero lignum est, contra naturam eius est comburi. V. Necessitas ex idea est, qua secundum ideam Dei aut hominis res ita se habent ut aliter habere nequeant. Hinc enim est quod duo et tria faciunt quinque, et numerus usque ad denarium progreditur apud nos, non autem apud omnes nationes. Nam non transit senarium apud quosdam Afros. Hinc etiam litterae et syllabae apud hanc aut illam gentem ita formantur et non aliter. Et haec necessitas concurrit quodammodo cum formali: sed quia potest se aliter habere ad placitum artificis, unde aliae nationes alias litteras et alia vocabula habent, idcirco non est necessitas intrinseca ut formalis.
